scope_allowed: Relevance of the quantities of interest

models.name: Model A: Anatomy-resolved explicit FE
models.what_it_computes: Time-resolved insertion force versus depth using a 3D subject-specific cochlear geometry with nonlinear contact, rate-dependent viscoelastic soft tissues, and Coulomb friction between electrode and cochlear walls.

models.name: Model B: Simplified explicit FE beam-in-shell
models.what_it_computes: Peak insertion force envelope and force–depth slope using a curvature-matched parametric cochlear shell and a beam representation of the electrode with aggregated contact/friction laws.

mechanisms.name: Lateral-wall frictional drag
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Sustained friction against the lateral wall dominates steady insertion force and correlates with risk of epithelial microtrauma.

mechanisms.name: Modiolus-side binding
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Intermittent contact with the modiolus produces transient force spikes that can precipitate tip deflection and inner-wall trauma.

mechanisms.name: Tip fold-over initiation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Onset of tip fold-over dramatically increases force and is linked to insertion failure and postoperative map instability.

mechanisms.name: Sheath/bucker sleeve buckling
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Local instability of guiding sleeves raises insertion force and can transfer load to delicate intracochlear structures.

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a 0–7 Credibility Index per (model × mechanism) pair, with 0 = no evidence and 7 = compelling evidence.

expected_decision.outcome_source: Under a preoperative planning Context of Use, the anatomy-resolved explicit FE model provides credible guidance for sustained lateral-wall drag and clinically useful hazard-flagging for modiolus-side binding and tip fold-over initiation.

name_keywords: TPR 0.78; timing offset 0.9 mm; amplitude error 11 mN
7/18 correct; onset error 3.7 mm; surge underprediction 45%

expected_context_of_use: The Context of Use is preoperative planning for adult candidates with standard cochlear anatomy imaged by high-resolution clinical CT (0.2–0.3 mm isotropic voxels).

spans: Subject-level geometries from 24 CT datasets and 18 phantom CAD files were meshed at 0.05–0.1 mm near-wall resolution, yielding stable contact surfaces.
A hierarchical Bayesian model tied friction priors (mean 0.26, SD 0.05) to phantom posteriors (mean 0.24, SD 0.04), with a credible 0.02 per mm/s dependence on speed.
findings.span: Subject-level geometries from 24 CT datasets and 18 phantom CAD files were meshed at 0.05–0.1 mm near-wall resolution, yielding stable contact surfaces.

spans: For Model A, halving the time step from 4.5e-7 s to 2.25e-7 s and doubling the contact penalty from 2.5 to 5.0 N/mm changed the sustained slope by 1.3% and the plateau by 0.9% across three representative phantoms (R=4.1, 4.3, 4.4 mm), and 1.6% and 1.1% in two cadaveric geometries.
findings.span: For Model A, halving the time step from 4.5e-7 s to 2.25e-7 s and doubling the contact penalty from 2.5 to 5.0 N/mm changed the sustained slope by 1.3% and the plateau by 0.9% across three representative phantoms (R=4.1, 4.3, 4.4 mm), and 1.6% and 1.1% in two cadaveric geometries.

spans: Across the 18 phantom insertions, the model reproduced sustained slopes with a mean absolute percentage error of 5.4% (95% CI 3.9–6.8%) and an RMSE of 8.7 mN.
The cadaver subset showed a median absolute error in sustained plateau of 9.6 mN (IQR 6.1–13.3 mN).
findings.span: Across the 18 phantom insertions, the model reproduced sustained slopes with a mean absolute percentage error of 5.4% (95% CI 3.9–6.8%) and an RMSE of 8.7 mN.

spans: In practice, when a predicted basal force plateau exceeds 60 mN for a given subject at 1.0 mm/s insertion speed, the plan may shift to a more lubricious regimen or slower advancement.
findings.span: In practice, when a predicted basal force plateau exceeds 60 mN for a given subject at 1.0 mm/s insertion speed, the plan may shift to a more lubricious regimen or slower advancement.

spans: Boundary and environmental realism was moderate.
Phantom tests were at room temperature (21–23 °C), whereas simulations used 35 °C tissue properties to align with cadaveric tests; this mismatch contributed to 10–14% systematic offsets.
findings.span: Boundary and environmental realism was moderate.

spans: In user workflow studies (n=20 simulated cases by six engineers), omission of the lumen smoothing step or misassignment of the round-window anchor produced basal misalignment and a 4–7 mN positive bias in sustained force; a gating checklist reduced such misconfigura-tions from 16% to 3%.
findings.span: In user workflow studies (n=20 simulated cases by six engineers), omission of the lumen smoothing step or misassignment of the round-window anchor produced basal misalignment and a 4–7 mN positive bias in sustained force; a gating checklist reduced such misconfigura-tions from 16% to 3%.

spans: We note that numerical code verification tasks were tracked during model development; these encompassed regression tests of contact formulations and beam/contact coupling in simplified geometries.

spans: Model B’s coarser mesh permitted a larger nominal step; halving the step to 6.0e-7 s altered the slope by 1.1% and the plateau by 0.8%.

spans: Model B, with its aggregated interface law, captured the population trend of sustained drag but showed larger case-to-case deviations: phantom slope error averaged 9.8% (95% CI 7.2–12.5%) with an RMSE of 13.9 mN.
Cadaveric sustained plateaus were matched within a median absolute error of 14.1 mN (IQR 10.2–17.7 mN).
findings.span: Model B, with its aggregated interface law, captured the population trend of sustained drag but showed larger case-to-case deviations: phantom slope error averaged 9.8% (95% CI 7.2–12.5%) with an RMSE of 13.9 mN.

spans: the automated fit of the parametric shell occasionally under-estimates the basal diameter if the round-window region is partially obscured on CT.

In a stress test (n=20 cases), this error mode occurred twice and produced a 5–8 mN positive force bias at 8–12 mm depth; an added warning threshold on basal diameter reduced the frequency in subsequent runs.
findings.span: the automated fit of the parametric shell occasionally under-estimates the basal diameter if the round-window region is partially obscured on CT.

spans: The bench-to-cadaver transition introduced environmental variability.
At 35 °C and in saline-lubricated cadavers, friction was lower than in room-temperature phantoms; the posterior distributions informed the simulations.
findings.span: The bench-to-cadaver transition introduced environmental variability.

spans: Operator workflow studies showed that inaccurate placement of the modiolar surface relative to the lumen center-line during segmentation could advance or delay predicted spike onset by up to 1.6 mm; re-segmentation with a standard protocol reduced such discrepancies.

spans: Model B lacks explicit inner-wall structure and instead employs a repulsive potential field to discourage beam proximity to the inner margin.
The simplified representation of the inner margin as a repulsive potential lacks the localized concavities and promi-nences that channel the electrode toward the modiolus.
findings.span: Model B lacks explicit inner-wall structure and instead employs a repulsive potential field to discourage beam proximity to the inner margin.

spans: We observed that automated fitting of the parametric shell can place the inner boundary slightly too far from the centerline in small cochleae, further attenuating inner-wall proximity.
A correction factor based on basal turn diameter alleviated the bias but did not restore the ability to predict spikes driven by localized anatomy.
findings.span: We observed that automated fitting of the parametric shell can place the inner boundary slightly too far from the centerline in small cochleae, further attenuating inner-wall proximity.

spans: The distal 3 mm of the electrode were modeled with a refined mesh (0.05 mm elements) and localized friction sampling to capture tip–wall interactions.
Variability in predictions was dominated by uncertainty in distal bending stiffness (±0.2 mN·mm2) and local friction (±0.03), with a smaller component due to segmentation noise at the apical turn.
findings.span: The distal 3 mm of the electrode were modeled with a refined mesh (0.05 mm elements) and localized friction sampling to capture tip–wall interactions.
